_note: Top-level *3 keys in the Widgy JSON -> which icon file to place in that key so on-device rendering is correct. The original Dark-Sky-order hypothesis (f3=clear-day, g3=clear-night, n3=partly-cloudy-day, o3=partly-cloudy-night) was FALSIFIED on-device 2026-08-29: Dallas ~1:14 PM CDT, condition 'Fair', native Weather 2 (Now) glyph showed a DAY symbol, yet the hero rendered clear-night.png (the g3 URL) - i.e. the daytime clear condition reads key g3. Day/night pairs are therefore stored night-first here (f3=clear-night, g3=clear-day, n3=partly-cloudy-night, o3=partly-cloudy-day). This placement fixes the observed bug under every candidate explanation (pair order flipped, whole list shifted by one, or Widgy's sunrise/sunset day-night selection inverted - Widgy release notes say day/night is decided by sunrise/sunset). Whether it is the true slot semantics or a compensating swap is UNRESOLVED: verify against a screenshot of Widgy's Weather (Custom Images) editor and correct here, then re-run build_widgy.py. Non-pair conditions (rain/snow/etc) kept as hypothesized; if on-device rain/cloud days ever showed a wrong icon, suspect the shifted-list theory and re-derive the whole map. null = unknown, left untouched.
